job.theme: the life of a famous Indian scientist

response.passage: Sir C.V. Raman was a brilliant Indian physicist who changed how we understand the world. Born in 1888 in Tiruchirappalli, he showed an early interest in science. In 1928, he discovered that when light passes through a transparent material, some of the deflected light changes its wavelength. This phenomenon, which occurs because the light molecules interact with the particles in the material, is now famously known as the Raman Effect. Because of this groundbreaking discovery, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930. Raman spent many years working at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Kolkata. He was deeply inspired by the blue color of the Mediterranean Sea during a voyage. He believed that science should be pursued with passion and curiosity. Raman's work proved that even simple observations could lead to major scientific breakthroughs. He remains an inspiration for millions of students across India who dream of exploring the mysteries of nature.
response.summary: Sir C.V. Raman was a famous Indian physicist known for his discovery of the Raman Effect. His work earned him the Nobel Prize and continues to inspire students today.
